newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan Motor sees 97/98 parent oper profit up 6.3%.
newsitem.headline: Nissan Motor sees 97/98 parent oper profit up 6.3%.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it expects its parent operating profit to rise 6.3 percent from a year earlier to 120 billion yen in fiscal 1997/98, ending on March 31, 1998.
Nissan, Japan's second largest carmaker, earlier on Tuesday reported an 81.2 percent gain in parent operating profit in fiscal 1996/97 to 112.9 billion yen.
"We want to achieve a group net profit of more than 100 billion yen in this business year," said Kanemitsu Anraku, a Nissan director.
He said Nissan expects its Mexican operation to break even in 1997/98, while its European unit, which was in the red during the last business year, is also expected to break even this year.
Nissan assumed exchange rates of 115 yen per dollar and 70 yen per mark in calculating its business forecasts for 1997/98, Anraku said.
Anraku said Nissan's profits would rise in 1997/98 due to rationalisation efforts, higher sales and a weak yen.

He also said Nissan plans parent capital expenditure in fiscal 1997/98 of 110 billion yen, up from 73.8 billion yen in the prior year, and group capital expenditure of 270 billion yen, up from 202.7 billion yen in 1996/97.
Parent research and development spending is expected to rise to 210 billion yen in 1997/98 from an actual 168 billion yen the year before, he added.

Nissan forecast domestic vehicle sales of 1.14 million units in 1997/98, up 1.2 percent year-on-year, while exports were seen rising 3.6 percent to 620,000 units and overseas production was projected to rise 2.0 percent to 1.1 million units, he said.
He added that Nissan Motor had not received requests from any organisation to assist failed Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co. Nissan Motor is Nissan Life's second-largest client.
